title: Transposon-derived open chromatin in human K562 cells is more active than other open chromatin in a reporter assay, but CRISPRi screens show no sign that it controls genes more often
abstract:
In human K562 cells, open chromatin that comes from transposable elements (TEs) is more active than other open chromatin when it is tested outside its genomic location in a reporter assay, but it does not control nearby genes more often when CRISPR interference silences it in its own location. This matters because about a quarter of human candidate regulatory elements come from TEs, and reporter activity is often used as evidence that TE-derived DNA has a regulatory function.

We used two public ENCODE data sets. The first has 14,734 CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) tests of element-gene pairs: 5,638 elements and 661 pairs in which silencing decreased the expression of the gene. The second is a lentivirus reporter assay (lentiMPRA) of about 114,000 K562 sequences of 200 bp. An element is TE-derived if one RepeatMasker TE copy covers at least half of it.

In the reporter assay, 46% of TE-derived open-chromatin sequences were active, against 38% of TE-free ones (odds ratio 1.54, 95% CI 1.37-1.72, after adjustment for GC content and clustering by TE subfamily). The excess came mostly from LTR retrotransposons (odds ratio 2.06). In the CRISPRi data, the odds ratio of a gene effect for TE-derived vs other elements, adjusted for chromatin marks, distance and screen, was 0.83 (0.60-1.17). It was 0.95 (0.68-1.33) when we also adjusted for whether the tested gene is ubiquitously expressed, and 0.96 (0.70-1.31) with five more cell types added. Effect sizes of positive pairs were similar (median decrease 11% vs 13%). So the data exclude a large excess of function for TE-derived elements but cannot separate equality from a small deficit. Closed-chromatin DNA from seven loci was as active in the reporter assay as shuffled control sequences (difference -0.7 percentage points, -3.1 to +1.3).

An independent review found that our pre-specified model adjusted for screen power, which depends on the outcome in this benchmark; the corrected estimates above replace it. Limits: 89% of positive pairs and all reporter data come from K562 cells; CRISPRi silences about 1 kb; young TE copies are rarely tested; the closed-chromatin sequences were selected for diverse chromatin signals. Prediction: in K562 cells, perturbation of reporter-active LTR-derived elements will change nearby genes no more often than perturbation of non-TE elements with the same chromatin marks, distance and target-gene type.

display.caption: A: TE origin increased the odds of reporter (lentiMPRA) activity, mostly through LTRs, but not the odds of a CRISPRi effect on a gene (main model 0.83, 0.60-1.17; with gene type 0.95). The two readouts come from different units and models. B: the fraction of elements with a CRISPRi effect rose with reporter activity for other elements and less clearly for TE-derived elements (unadjusted; interaction p = 0.08).

Odds ratio of a CRISPRi effect for TE-derived vs other elements in selected analyses. Grey: the pre-specified model, which is invalid because its power covariate depends on the outcome. The corrected estimates include 1 and exclude a large excess.

Fraction of 200-bp sequences active in the K562 lentiMPRA (above the 95th percentile of 247 shuffled controls). Closed-chromatin DNA from 7 diversity-selected loci was about as active as shuffled DNA; TE-derived open chromatin was the most active.
